Activation and regulation mechanisms of STING‐induced cellular senescence

Activation and regulation mechanisms of STING‐induced cellular senescence. Chromatin fragments, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction (leading to mtDNA release), and retroviruses can trigger cGAS‐STING‐mediated cellular senescence and SASPs. Several regulators are involved in the regulation of STING‐induced senescence. Nuclear cGAS promotes TRIM41‐mediated ubiquitination and degradation of ORF2p, thus inhibiting LINE1 retrotransposition to maintain genome stability. TXNRD1 is a cytoplasmic chromatin fragment‐localized protein that promotes cGAS activity. YAP/TAZ directly regulates lamin B1 and ACTR2 transcription to prevent the release of nuclear DNA fragments. Non‐canonical pathways are involved in the cGAS‐STING‐mediated induction of SASPs. IRF3 interacts with RB to block RB hyperphosphorylation and E2F transcription, thus promoting senescence. In addition, STING/PERK/eIF2α signaling and STING/PERK/NF‐κB signaling also participate in STING‐induced cellular senescence. ACTR2, actin‐related protein 2; cGAS, cyclic GMP‐AMP synthase; E2F, early 2 factor; eIF2α, eukaryotic initiation factor 2 alpha; IRF3, IFN regulatory factor 3; LINE1, long interspersed nuclear element‐1; mtDNA, mitochondrial DNA; NF‐κB, nuclear transcription factor‐kappa B; ORF2p, open reading frame 2 protein; PERK, protein kinase RNA‐like endoplasmic reticulum kinase; RB, retinoblastoma protein; SASPs, senescence‐associated secretory phenotypes; STING, stimulator of interferon gene; TRIM41, tripartite motif‐containing protein 41; TXNRD1, thioredoxin reductase 1; Ub, ubiquitination; YAP/TAZ, Yes‐associated protein/Transcriptional coactivator with PDZ‐binding motif
